SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS COLLEGE, THREE PRINTED VOLUMES, 1941-1943
Camp Otoreke in the college calendar; the YMCA Fellowship students in the yearbooks

Found 2026-09-07 by the accounted whole-corpus sweep of the Internet Archive
collection `rma-concordia-publications` (16,491 text items) under p_479. None of
the three items appears in sources.json; the collection's Kanawana/Otoreke hits
are otherwise the YMCA fonds material this project already holds.

  A. "Faculty of Arts, Science and Commerce Announcement 1941-1942"
     identifier 1941-1942 | 171,462 chars | the college's printed calendar
  B. "The Annual Yearbook 1942"  identifier 1942-the-annual-yearbook | 228,830
  C. "The Annual Yearbook 1943"  identifier 1943-the-annual-yearbook | 191,404

Term counts, run rather than assumed: Otoreke A=5 B=2 C=1; KANAWANA A=0 B=0 C=0;
Fellowship A=1 B=8 C=11; Hupfield A=0 B=1 C=2; Barker A=0 B=1 C=5.
Kanawana itself is absent from all three. What these documents carry is Otoreke
and the Fellowship, and the Fellowship is why they matter to Kanawana.

===============================================================================
A. THE COLLEGE CALENDAR, 1941-42: CAMP OTOREKE IS AN INDEXED ENTRY
===============================================================================

Printed in the body, immediately after the paragraph on the Canadian Officers'
Training Corps and the 110 hours of basic military training:

  "COLLEGE WEEK AT CAMP OTOREKE. During the first week of September the Y.M.C.A.
  Camp Otoreke is reserved for former and prospective students of the College and
  members of the faculty. This activity offers students and staff an excellent
  opportunity for informal fellowship. Registrations for the week at Camp Otoreke
  will be accepted at the college office during the month of August, until
  August 22nd."

And twice in the index at the back:

  "Camp Otoreke; college week .... 14"
  "Otoreke, Camp .... 14"

The calendar also locates the college itself: "Sir George Williams College, which
occupies the second and third floors of the Drummond Street Y.M.C.A. building.
Accommodation is available for 2,500 students."

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A NOTICE. A university calendar is the document a college
uses to state what it formally offers. Camp Otoreke is in it, indexed, with a
registration deadline and a booking channel through the college office -- not
the Y's. The site was reserved for the college for a named week each September,
open to alumni, prospective students and faculty. wiki/site/camp-otoreke.md has
off-season and conference use of the site from other angles; this is the college
end of the same arrangement, printed by the college.

===============================================================================
B. THE 1942 YEARBOOK: RON HUPFIELD, "DIRECTOR OF 'Y' CAMP OTOREKE"
===============================================================================

His graduating entry, transcribed as printed (the OCR's stray characters for the
apostrophe-year abbreviations are regularised to ' here; nothing else is changed):

  "RON HUPFIELD  ARTS
   Activities: Y.M.C.A. Fellowship student. 'Y' handball champion, '39 & '41;
   Pres. of Fellowship Men, '40, '41; Chairman, Relig. Educ. Council of Que.
   '38, '39; Sec'y. North Branch 'Y' '40-'41; Mgr. Strathcona Hall, '41 & '42;
   DIRECTOR OF 'Y' CAMP OTOREKE; Sec'y. Y.M.C.A. Ski Club; Asst. Young Men's
   Sec'y., Central Y.M.C.A. '39-'40.
   Future Plans: To go into full-time Y.M.C.A. secretaryship upon graduation."

THIS CONTRADICTS A SENTENCE IN wiki/site/camp-otoreke.md AND THE ARTICLE MUST BE
CORRECTED. That article's Hupfield paragraph concludes that he "does not appear
on the Montreal staff at all until 1947 and is never placed at Otoreke by any
source held here," and on that basis rejects a camp blog's account of "Ron and
Valma Huppfield" running the camp during the Second World War as chronology that
is "not attested." The yearbook attests it. Hupfield was Director of Camp
Otoreke by his graduation in 1942, and held Association posts continuously from
1938: Religious Education Council of Quebec chairman '38-'39, Assistant Young
Men's Secretary at Central '39-'40, Secretary of North Branch '40-'41, Manager
of Strathcona Hall '41-'42.

BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT WAS WRONG. The clause "never placed at Otoreke by any
source held here" was true of the sources held when it was written and is the
correctly hedged half. "Does not appear on the Montreal staff at all until 1947"
is the half that overreached: it is a statement about the annual reports, which
list appointments to branch secretaryships, generalised into a statement about
the man. A student holding the Strathcona Hall managership and a branch
secretaryship while enrolled at the college would not be in those lists. The
blog's chronology was right and the annual reports were the wrong instrument for
testing it.

Also in the 1942 yearbook, among the advertisements:

  "VACATION TIME IS CALLING YOU! / CAMP OTOREKE / An ideal vacation spot in the
  heart of the Laurentians for young men, young women and young married couples.
  Open June 6th to Sept. 7th -- Canoeing, swimming, tennis, etc. CAMPER-PLANNED
  RECREATION. Low Rates. INFORMATION FROM YOUR LOCAL Y.M.C.A. A HOLIDAY YOU'LL
  NEVER FORGET."

Three things in six lines: the 1942 season's exact dates; the market stated as
young men, young women AND YOUNG MARRIED COUPLES, which is a different clientele
from a boys' camp; and the phrase "camper-planned recreation" as a selling point
in 1942 -- twenty-four years before A. Ross Seaman described Kanawana's
programme to the Montreal YMCA's 1966-67 annual report as a "participatory
democracy" with campers planning their own activities. The idea has a longer
local pedigree than this wiki has been giving it, and it was in an advertisement,
which means it was expected to attract rather than to puzzle.

===============================================================================
C. THE 1943 YEARBOOK: THE FELLOWSHIP, FROM THE INSIDE
===============================================================================

  "GEORGE N. BARKER  ARTS
   Activities: President S.C.M. Group '41-'42, National Council representative
   '43, Member Clubs Com. '42.
   Other Activities: DIR. OTOREKE SKI LODGE '43, Executive Fellowship
   Secretaries Group '43, Member Montreal Christian Youth Com. '42-'43.
   Former Education: Graduate Newmarket High School, graduate International
   Accountants Society Inc.
   Sports: All sports especially handball, skiing, canoe tripping.
   Hobbies: Music, photography, reading, discussions.
   Future Plans: Y.M.C.A. war services, P. Graduate studies someday, (I hope)."

  "MacARTHUR PAT. GORDON  ARTS
   Activities: S.C.M., Debating Society, Publications Committee, Military
   Training Corps, Interyear Basketball, Volleyball.
   Interests: In all students problems, PRACTICE OF DEMOCRATIC METHOD IN ALL
   STUDENT AFFAIRS, extra curricular activities that help students relate
   themselves to problems of every day living.
   Former Education: Graduate of Kingston C.[V].I. (Honour Matriculation), two
   years Technical School, one year Queens University.
   Other Information: Y.M.C.A. SECRETARY IN TRAINING, developed interest in Y.
   work in Kingston, Ontario in 1938 while preparing for a Science Course,
   Acting Boys Work Secretary at the Kgn. Y.M.C.A. before coming to Mtl. in
   1941. HAVE BEEN MTL. FELLOWSHIP SECRETARY FOR 2 YEARS, with Central Branch
   doing Hi-Y & Gra-Y club work and in Rosemont Community doing Community Boys
   Work.
   Hobbies: Amateur radio.
   Future Plans: Work with Y.M.C.A. War Services overseas, Y.M.C.A. civilian
   work as soon as war situation permits."

  "MURRAY B. SHANTZ  ARTS
   Activities: Georgian basketball team, S.C.M., FELLOWSHIP STUDENT.
   Office: President S.C.M. 1943, SEC'Y FELLOWSHIP 1942.
   Former Education: St. Catharines Collegiate Institute.
   Outside Interests: Looking after ....
   Future Plans: Rather inclined to think that the government will help me to
   decide this."

And the Fellowship as a body, from the athletics and social pages of both years:

  1942: "The first volleyball game of the year was played between Dr. Norris'
  Faculty Team and Mac Singleton's Fellowship men... The Fellowship team also
  played Oscar Pearson's Central 'Y' Business Men and Archie Crystal's Science
  Men."

  1943: "Dr. Norris and his professorial proteges started the ball bouncing this
  year by taking the over confident Fellowship aspirants down a peg or two."

  1943: "The Fellowship students were very ambitious boys this year, taking a
  SIX WEEK COURSE IN CLASS GYMNASTICS. Each of the members of the group
  contributed to the instruction of the course and benefitted greatly through
  this mutual co-operation."

  1943, at the athletic awards night: "Voluntary waiters for the occasion were
  the versatile Fellowship students under the able guidance of head-waiter
  G. N. Barker."

  1943 basketball: "Players:- L. Welton, M. Shantz, S. Armstrong, G. Wood,
  A. Ulrich, G. Higgins, R. Jonas, M. Ram, H. Rocklin, C. Gursky, and
  N. Fouriezos, Manager."

===============================================================================
WHAT THIS SETTLES, CHECKED AGAINST THE DESTINATION FIRST
===============================================================================

1. WHAT "YMCA FELLOWSHIP SECRETARY" MEANT. Concordia's obituary of A. Ross
   Seaman, found earlier the same day, says "Ross's history at Concordia goes
   back to the 1940s when he attended Sir George as a YMCA Fellowship
   Secretary," and the note written on it could only say that he was on the
   Association's payroll and in the classroom at once. Gordon's entry says what
   the arrangement was, in the first person and in the same years: "Y.M.C.A.
   Secretary in training... Have been Mtl. Fellowship Secretary for 2 years,
   with Central Branch doing Hi-Y & Gra-Y club work and in Rosemont Community
   doing Community Boys Work." It was a paid apprenticeship in the secretaryship,
   worked in the branches, with the college attendance as its academic half.

2. THE FELLOWS WERE A COHORT, NOT A CATEGORY. They fielded a volleyball team
   under a captain, taught each other a six-week gymnastics course, waited
   tables at the awards night under one of their own, elected a president and a
   secretary of their own body ("Pres. of Fellowship Men" 1940 and 1941;
   "sec'y Fellowship 1942"), and had an "Executive Fellowship Secretaries Group"
   by 1943.

3. IT JOINS UP WITH SOMETHING THIS WIKI ALREADY HAD. wiki/people/murray-shantz.md
   quotes the Montreal YMCA's 1943 annual report: "Murray Shantz, George Barker,
   Gordon Patrick and Lloyd Welton complete their Training Fellowships" -- the
   scheme for "young men looking to the Assn. secretaryship as a career." THREE
   OF THOSE FOUR NAMES ARE IN THIS YEARBOOK as Sir George students in 1943:
   Shantz and Barker under their own entries, Welton on the basketball team
   beside Shantz. So the association's Training Fellowship and enrolment at Sir
   George Williams College were the same thing seen from two ends, and the wiki
   held both ends without the join.

   A CAUTION ON THE FOURTH NAME. The annual report's "Gordon Patrick" and the
   yearbook's "MacArthur Pat. Gordon" may well be one man with the name
   inverted, and the biographies fit -- both are Y secretaries in training in
   Montreal in 1943. THIS IS NOT ASSERTED. It is a plausible identification
   needing a third document, and it is written into the wiki as a question, not
   a fact.

4. TWO NAMED OTOREKE OFFICERS THE ARCHIVE'S FINDING AID DOES NOT NAME.
   Hupfield as Director of the camp by 1942, and Barker as "Dir. Otoreke Ski
   Lodge '43." wiki/site/camp-otoreke.md's Ski Lodge section is built from
   Concordia's finding aid sub-series P145/12H, which lists files -- a
   "Memorandum proposing ski club. - 1941," correspondence, committee wants --
   without naming who ran the thing. Barker is a name in the gap, in a year the
   file list covers only as paper.

5. AND A LINE OF DESCENT WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD. The 1943 Fellowship cohort
   produced Murray B. Shantz, who directed Kamp Kanawana in the mid-1950s, and
   George N. Barker, who ran the Otoreke ski lodge the year they graduated. The
   camps were staffed by the college and the college was inside the Y's own
   building. This is the concrete machinery behind the institutional argument in
   wiki/connections/institutional-lineage/sgw-concordia-connection.md.
